title: Australia’s east coast deluged by storms as roads flood and damaging winds forecast for NSW and Victoria
summary: Severe weather and flood watch warnings are in place as a storm band moves from central Queensland through NSW to Victoria and Tasmania Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The final weekend of Australia’s wettest spring on record for an El Niño year is delivering a deluge of storms and heavy rain. title: ‘I told it to never call me again’: AI bots wreak havoc with UK restaurant bookings
summary: Meta claims its Muse assistant will make users’ lives easier, but business owners say AI is driving them to go analogue Restaurant owners are battling a horde of AI bots and returning to using the telephone instead of online booking as new virtual assistants launch in the UK – but sometimes even that isn’t enough to stop them. This week, Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it shop and make restaurant reservations. The bot is given access to the user’s email if they give it permission, and it can make restaurant bookings and go shopping on the user’s behalf. Continue reading...

title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
summary: Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed him They are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals. But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault , 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company. Continue reading...

title: Stunted sprouts: heatwaves and drought take toll on festive vegetable
summary: The Christmas staple is smaller this year after a hot, dry summer hit the water-loving – but versatile – brassica They are a key ingredient in many Christmas dinners, but brussels sprouts appearing on diners’ plates this festive season are likely to be smaller than usual, after the hot, dry summer took its toll on the water-loving crop. Sprouts are generally planted outdoors between March and early June, meaning they were already in the ground when the UK faced a series of heatwaves and drought conditions across Wales and most of England. title: Mental health patients refusing NHS treatment over shared therapy notes
summary: Exclusive: Uploading of intimate psychiatric information to wider medical records prompts some to shun support altogether Some psychiatric patients are refusing treatment over the NHS adding intimate details from therapy sessions to their medical notes, fuelling fears that breaching privacy is posing a risk to health, the Guardian can reveal. One stopped medical care for a heart condition when he discovered that details of intrusive sexual thoughts he’d experienced as result of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) had been shared with a cardiac nurse. Continue reading...

title: Unpaid TV licence or cycling on pavement could bar people from settling in UK
summary: Exclusive: New immigration rules will introduce strict threshold where any adult conviction triggers mandatory refusal People could be barred from settling in the UK over minor infractions such as cycling on the pavement or failing to pay a TV licence, ministers have been warned before the introduction of new “earned settlement” rules. Under the plans, which are to come into effect next year, securing indefinite leave to remain will become significantly harder for many people. The rules introduce a strict new threshold where any adult conviction resulting in a court disposal – including fines, community orders, conditional cautions, and absolute or conditional discharges – triggers mandatory refusal. Continue reading...

title: Palestinian tells of ‘devastating’ struggle after being made redundant by EU in Gaza
summary: Mohammad Baraka unable to access redundancy pay for almost 20 years’ service as family’s situation becomes ‘increasingly desperate’ A Palestinian man who worked for the EU in Gaza has told of a “devastating” struggle to survive after he was made redundant by bosses in Brussels. He was let go last year after being evacuated to Egypt but his redundancy payment was made to an account to which he has no access. “My family’s situation has become increasingly desperate,” said Mohammad Baraka, a former staffer at the EU border assistance mission (EUBam). title: Yuri and I used to play football together. Then I spotted his name among Russia’s war dead
summary: I had no idea he had gone to fight in Ukraine and without hacked data I would probably never have learned of his death One evening, after weeks spent counting Russia’s war dead, I began looking for names I might recognise. My colleagues and I had been working our way through more than 11m death certificates leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, and identifying nearly half a million Russian soldiers who had died in the war in Ukraine.
